svg.title: Propose, guard, approve, apply: the four stages a cluster change passes through
svg.desc: Four numbered stages run left to right in equal columns. Stage one, Propose, sits on the client side of a dashed protocol boundary: the model picks a tool and fills the arguments, shown as a call to scale_deployment on the checkout deployment with five hundred replicas, and a note that the approval parameter is not among them because Resolve strips it from the published schema, leaving the model no field in which to grant its own permission. Stage two, Guard, is the first thing on the server side: a resolver running guard_namespace and guard_replicas before anything is shown to anyone, where a pass means ask a human and a raise ends the call without rendering a question. Stage three, Approve, builds the preview from the arguments and nothing else, returns a result whose type is input_required, ends the original request holding no state, and waits for the client to ask a person and retry with a new identifier and the answer. Stage four, Apply and verify, sends the scale patch, reads the object back so that the requested and observed replica counts sit side by side, and returns the same preview object that was in the question. A red arrow drops out of the guard stage, before stage three, into a band along the bottom: out of bounds means no question is ever shown, the refusal reads that scaling to five hundred is refused because the configured maximum is twenty, stages three and four never run, and the test whose user always approves asserts that it saw no question and that no cluster call was recorded.
svg.text: The guard runs before the question is rendered, so nobody approves a change the server was always going to refuse.
in which to grant its own.
Out of bounds: no question is ever shown
Refusing to scale to 500. The configured maximum is 20.
Stages 3 and 4 never run. The test's user always approves, and never got the chance:
The approval parameter never reaches the model, and the preview that was approved is the object that comes back.
